Hi Asha —

Appreciate the clear recap — that helps. Below are realistic options and constraints from our side. I attached a short PDF that summarizes the options (redwood-data-retention-options.pdf).

Short answers first: yes, we can support a 0-retention pilot for chat and KV cache (ephemeral-only), and we can provide 90-day audit logs, with the caveat that audit logs and system traces are considered operational data and may include minimal metadata. For strongest guarantees we recommend Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) or a Dedicated deployment with customer-managed logging.

Options (high-level):
1) Redwood Hosted (fastest onboarding)
   - Ephemeral request handling: we can enable a short-log profile where conversational payloads are not written to persistent storage and KV caches are in-memory only.
   - Audit logs: by default stored in our internal observability for 30 days. We can route audit logs to a customer-owned S3 and configure 90-day retention as a special configuration for enterprise deals.
   - Residency: pick region (us-east or eu-west). Persisted logs follow region selection.

2) Redwood Dedicated (reserved capacity)
   - Customer gets isolated GPU pool and ability to request audit logs exported to customer S3 with custom retention controls (90 days possible).
   - Ephemeral profile available; same caveat about model internal telemetry.

3) Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem)
   - Full control: Voyant can keep all persisted telemetry in customer-managed storage. We can disable any persistent chat logging and only keep ephemeral in-memory caches.
   - Best for strict 0-retention guarantees for user content.

Technical notes / constraints:
- Redaction: we can run pre-ingestion PII masking as a preprocess, or provide a redaction webhook that runs prior to any write. This adds ~50–200ms to request latency depending on rules.
- Audit logs: we can export a superset of metadata (request id, timestamp, route, model variant) to customer S3. Full request payload export is configurable but for Voyant’s 90-day ask we recommend exporting only metadata + hashed identifiers and keeping raw payloads out of the exported logs.
- Model outputs: note that some downstream tooling (e.g., model explainers) may buffer outputs; these are included in our standard observability unless you opt-out or route them to customer storage.

Pilot proposal (minimal):
- Duration: 2 weeks (scope limited to one route, up to 100k tokens/day).
- Profile: ephemeral request handling + audit log export to customer S3 (90d retention) + pre-ingestion redaction hook.
- Deliverables: config doc, checklist for security team, short SOC2 snapshot (attached).

Next step: can you confirm whether Voyant would prefer Hosted with custom logging export or Redwood Private for the pilot? I’ve cc’d Marissa from our security/solutions team — she can help scope an SOW and provide the export playbook.

Hi Asha —

Quick technical clarification from infra/serving side (copied from our internal playbook):

- Pre-ingestion redaction: we can orchestrate a synchronous redaction step (redaction service runs in the same request path) and we will not commit any payload to persistent logs until the redaction service returns success. If redaction fails, the request returns 5xx and nothing is persisted. This meets the "fail to block persistence" requirement.

- Audit log export: we will write audit events to an encrypted write-ahead log in the serving zone, then stream to a configured S3 bucket using server-side encryption (SSE-KMS) and a customer-managed KMS key if requested. Partitioning: yyyy/mm/dd/requestid, lifecycle rule: transition to IA at 30 days, expire after 90 days. We can provide a sample IAM policy for the bucket.

- Hashing vs reversible identifiers: we can ship both. By default we will include hashed user ids; if Voyant wants reversible mapping Voyant can control keys (via KMS) and we will write encrypted identifiers that Voyant can decrypt.

I attached a short SOC2 snapshot to accelerate your review. Also — note that if you want absolute zero chance of provider-side persisted copies, Redwood Private or an on-prem option is the recommended path.
